raw_text: [[File:{{{Alt}}}|28px|link=]] For the troops, see Baby Dragon and Dragon . "Locked away for his anger issues, this tanky Flying Hero gets madder and mightier when separated from Friendly Flying units . His royal rampage boosts damage by 100%, attack speed by 50%, and reduces damage taken from traps . When defending, he can only be attacked by air-targeting enemies." Contents 1 Summary 2 Strategies 2.1 Offensive Strategies 2.2 Defensive Strategies 3 Statistics 4 Hero Equipments 5 History 6 Hero Skins 6.1 Skin Availability 6.2 Dragon Duke Skins 6.3 Dragon Duke Skin Features 6.4 Notes 7 Audio 7.1 General 7.2 Dialogue 8 Gallery 8.1 Images 8.2 Concept Art 9 Trivia 9.1 General 9.2 Comparisons Summary [ ] The Dragon Duke is the second aerial Hero and the sixth overall in terms of release who attacks all targets from melee range, introduced on March 1, 2026. He is unlocked by upgrading the Hero Hall to level 9, which requires Town Hall 15. As a Hero, the Dragon Duke can participate in both attack and defense, but will not be available to use if he is being upgraded. Like other Heroes, he is not upgraded in the Laboratory but rather upgraded with a Builder . On his default skin, the Dragon Duke otherwise appears similar to a Dragon , except he is larger and bulkier, with a crimson body and a thistle-colored underside. He has orange eyes, thistle eyebrows, three short, thick yellow horns on top of his head (two of them being curved and parallelepiped and the center being shorter and flatter), and yellow rectangular plates on his back. The bottom part of his mouth is also thistle-colored, with a similar layout to the Electro Dragon but with spikes on some parts. He also has a pair of handcuffs tied on his wrists and metal chains held by a golden lock in the center. Like the Minion Prince , the Dragon Duke will defend the village when assigned to a Hero Banner . The Dragon Duke only defends his territory around his banner and will retreat if lured too far out. He does not need to be defeated for an attack to end in a 3-star. When defending, the Dragon Duke will fly, making him unreachable by units that only target ground such as the Barbarian King . He can neither use his passive ability nor use his Hero Equipment during this time. As a Hero, the Dragon Duke has an ability that can be used once per battle which allows him to recover some of his health, with the amount increasing every fifth level. The Hero Equipment that he wields may add additional effects to the ability or a unique passive effect, on top of various passive stats increase. When unlocked, the Dragon Duke starts with the Fire Heart and Flame Blower. The Fire Heart allows the Dragon Duke to create a large death explosion. It gives a passive increase to damage and max health, and grants him self healing. The Flame Blower creates a cone of fire forward from the Dragon Duke and deals significant damage, similar to the Baby Dragon in the Builder Base, and grants an increased health recovery. It gives a passive increase to maximum health. Upgrading the Blacksmith to level 9 and 10 unlocks the Stun Blaster and Electro Fangs, respectively. The Stun Blaster creates a stunning shockwave around the Dragon Duke that stuns and damages buildings and defending troops except resource buildings and Walls , and grants an increased health recovery. It gives a passive increase to damage and maximumm health. The Electro Fangs allows the Dragon Duke's regular attacks to gain the chain lightning effect, jumping to additional targets beyond the Duke's original target. It gives a passive increase to maximum health. The Dragon Duke has a passive ability known as the Royal Rampage, that allows him to deal twice the damage and attack 1.5 times faster when he is by himself without other air units within 6 tiles, effectively dealing thrice the normal damage per second, the same as the Baby Dragon , but also reduces the damage from traps by 20%. He attacks by either clawing the target when aerial units are within 6 tiles of him, or breathing fire on it when rampaging. This ability is not disabled by the Dragon Duke's Pet if it is flying, like the Angry Jelly , but flying Pets from other Heroes will disable this ability. Summoned units from Pets (like Boogers from Sneezy ) can disable this ability. If the Dragon Duke is defeated while his Pet survives, that Pet will no longer be considered his own for this particular interaction; if the Dragon Duke is revived later by a Revive Spell , his Pet can disable the ability. The Phoenix does not disable the Royal Rampage ability when she hatches and revives the Dragon Duke, but only while her ability is active. Strategies [ ] Offensive Strategies [ ] The six Home Village Heroes serve different roles in raids. The Barbarian King is the strength specialist, the Minion Prince is the air specialist, the Archer Queen is the speed specialist, the Grand Warden is the support specialist, the Royal Champion is the offense specialist, and the Dragon Duke is the solo specialist. When alone, the Dragon Duke can prove to be a very powerful Hero, able to destroy a compartment by himself with the help of his Flame Blower or Stun Blaster and Fire Heart , depending on the strategy. He is also resistant to trap damage, allowing him to endure Seeking Air Mines with ease. Be careful, as a single air unit (like Minions and Balloons ) can disable this ability, so keep in mind. By far the most common Pets to use with the Dragon Duke are the Phoenix and the Angry Jelly . The former allows the Dragon Duke to resurrect him temporarily, especially when he is equipped with the Fire Heart's ability to deal huge amounts of damage, especially when sent alone. The latter pet allows the Dragon Duke to specifically target defenses temporarily, which can be a viable option for destroying major defenses, and can sometimes be paired with Lightning and Earthquake Spells . These aerial Pets will not disable the Dragon Duke's passive ability. Other aerial Pets can be used, like the Greedy Raven and the Electro Owl , but the former only targets resource buildings while the latter cannot keep up with the Dragon Duke. Do not use Sneezy with him, as this will disable his Royal Rampage, rendering him vulnerable to aerial traps via her Boogers . In air attacks involving Dragons , Dragon Riders , Electro Dragons , or a combination of these, he is treated as a tank for those units (similar to the Lava Hound ), usually paired with the Minion Prince and the Grand Warden set to Air mode. Their high hitpoints can protect him from taking too much damage, but due to his shorter range, he may be exposed to aerial traps , but he can also protect them in return. He may not use his Royal Rampage ability, but with the Stun Blaster , he can prevent major defenses from dealing damage to the army, especially single-target Inferno Towers , Monoliths , and Revenge Towers from taking them down, provided if used correctly. Be mindful of the defending Dragon Duke, as he is untargetable by units which target ground. Use Dragons, Baby Dragons, the Archer Queen , the Royal Champion , or other units that target air to knock him out of battle, owing to his extremely high hitpoints. As the Dragon Duke is one of the Heroes with the highest hitpoints, using Revive Spells when he is knocked out can be extremely powerful as they allow him to continually wreak havoc onto the base, increasing the chances of a successful attack. He can become overwhelmed by swarms like Skeletons from Witches and Skeleton Traps , as he attacks one target at a time, even when using his fiery breath. However, this does not happen if he still has his Ability. The Flame Blower is able to take out all the Skeletons in front of him. The Stun Blaster deals enough damage to take out the Skeletons in a huge radius. And the Rocket Backpack not only takes out the Skeletons, but also causes the Dragon Duke to fly to the other side of the map. Defensive Strategies [ ] Aerial traps like Seeking Air Mines are not as effective when the Dragon Duke is alone. However, if the attacker accidentally places an aerial unit near him, this disables his Royal Rampage ability, allowing the Seeking Air Mines to significantly damage him if not knock him out of battle. Clan Castle troops like Super Minions and Inferno Dragons can deal significant damage to the Dragon Duke, allowing them to eventually defeat him. However, this would take a while to do so, which means that they will eventually get taken out by him. Since the Dragon Duke is a single-target Hero, Witches can summon Skeletons that distract and eventually overwhelm him, buying time for defenses to quickly deal damage to him before he does too much damage to the base. However, if he has the Flame Blower ability still active, the attacker can use it to destroy the Witches and damage any nearby buildings, rendering it useless. It is only when it was already used does the strategy work on him. The Stun Blaster can also work in this regard, because it also stuns the Witches, allowing the Dragon Duke to take them out. The Barbarian King and the Dragon Duke work together in defending against ground and air units. While the Barbarian King may not target air units, he can tank the damage while the Dragon Duke deals with them. Against ground targets, the Dragon Duke can deal with them without being damaged, unless if units that target air are in the main army, where he would tank the damage. Skins are divided into three classes: Gold denotes a skin that was featured as a Gold Pass skin in Season Challenges . All Hero Skins from the Gold Pass since April 2023 have been available as the first reward on the Gold track. Prior to this, they have all been the last reward on the Gold track unless specified. All Gold skins are available permanently for purchase at a price of 1,500 Gems exactly a year after the skin was originally offered in the Gold Pass. Once available in the Shop, they may also be found in Legendary-rated Treasure Chests after the loot pool is refreshed in game updates. Standard and Legendary denotes skins not available from the Gold Pass that were available only through a special offer or event. Unless otherwise stated in the notes, these skins' special offers were available in the season listed, and cost the equivalent of $3.99 USD for Standard skins, or $9.99 USD for Legendary skins. The notes section may also include additional context of an offer. Skin from collaboration are not available for re-purchase in the Cosmetics tab. Key for highlighted entries: Entries that are highlighted denote that the skin is available in the current Season Challenges season. Entries marked with a Coathanger denote a Standard or Legendary skin that is permanently available for re-purchase in the cosmetics tab at the original price when the skin was originally offered. Entries marked with a Gem denote that the skin is purchasable with Gems; all skins currently purchasable in this manner cost 1,500 . Entries marked with a Yellow Star denote that the skin is exclusive; these skins will not be available for re-purchase in the future. Dragon Duke hesitates Gallery [ ] Images [ ] Info image Concept Art [ ] Concepts design of Dragon Duke Concepts for the Equipment Trivia [ ] General [ ] At the end of the February Wise Warriors medal event, a lock and some chains are shown, teasing the existence of the Dragon Duke, similar to previous medal event having an object that teases the theme of the next one. Before the Dragon Duke is released, most of the UI that for it is grayed out. When tapping on buttons that leads to more information about the Hero, it will show a red warning message like " Breaking loose soon! " and " Imprisoned! Coming to Hero Hall Level 9 soon! ". The only information released on the February 22, 2026 sneak peek is his appearance, the look of his Equipment, which Town Hall and Hero Hall he is unlocked at, and a description in the Chief's Journey ("A tough and fiery Hero who fights better alone."). Strangely, despite being based on the Dragon , the Dragon Duke's attacks seems to lack splash damage as opposed to the regular Dragon, whose attacks deal splash damage in a small radius. Comparisons [ ] The Dragon Duke is one of the Heroes that can fly, the others being the Grand Warden , Minion Prince , and Battle Copter . Despite being a Dragon, his passive ability is the same as the Baby Dragon , with an extra bonus of trap damage reduction. His equipment is same as the other Dragons' abilities. The Fire Heart provides a lethal death damage explosion when the Duke is defeated, functioning similarly to the Dragon Rider damage upon death, although with a much bigger radius. The Flame Blower is an exact copy of the Fiery Sneeze ability from the Baby Dragon in Builder Base, although with much more range and damage. The Electro Fangs grants a chain lightning effect on every strike, similiar to Electro Dragon . The Dragon Duke is the second non-human Hero in the game, the first being the Minion Prince. The Dragon Duke is the only Hero in the game which he is maxed out for the first week alongside his Equipment when released to all players before the update. In addition, his Hero Skin, the Imprisoned Duke skin, was released at the same time he was released. The Dragon Duke is the first and currently the only Hero in the game to have a passive ability of his own, that activates when he is on offense if there are no other aerial units nearby. The Dragon Duke is the Hero with the least amount of levels in the Home Village, with 25. The Dragon Duke is the first Hero in the game with an alliterated name. Unlike other Heroes, the Dragon Duke does not have any Equipment that summons troops (eg: puppets). This is most likely due to his ability being disabled when summoned aerial troops are nearby, effectively reducing his overall power.
